standard.title: Retell using plot and language
standard.description: orally retell or adapt a familiar story using plot and characters, language features including vocabulary, and structure of a familiar text, through role-play, writing, drawing or digital tools
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can retell and adapt familiar literary texts through play, performance, images or writing at Foundation level (AC9EFLE05). They have not yet deliberately drawn on plot, character, vocabulary choices and text structure as resources for retelling — the Year 1 expectation makes these elements explicit as tools.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students orally retell or adapt a familiar story using plot and characters, appropriate vocabulary and text structure, through role-play, writing, drawing or digital tools.

nodes.label: Retelling the plot in order
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can orally retell the main events of a familiar story in sequence, including the key characters, problem and resolution.
nodes.minimum_width: Retell the main events of a familiar story in order, including who is involved and how the problem is resolved.
nodes.typical_width: Orally retell a familiar story using plot sequence (beginning, middle, end with problem and resolution), naming key characters and describing their roles.
wider: Retell stories from multiple texts, comparing how different plots are structured
Retell a story from a different character's perspective — how does the plot feel different?
success_criteria: Student retells events in sequence without major omissions or reversals
Student includes the problem and its resolution in their retelling

nodes.label: Using language features in retelling
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can use language features from the original text — vocabulary, dialogue, descriptive phrases — in their retelling.
nodes.minimum_width: Incorporate at least two vocabulary items or language features from the original text into an oral retelling.
nodes.typical_width: Use vocabulary, descriptive phrases and where appropriate, dialogue from the original text in retelling, showing awareness that language choices shape how the story is told.
wider: Compare a retelling that uses the original vocabulary with one that substitutes everyday language — discuss how word choices affect the story
Experiment with adding new vocabulary to enrich the retelling beyond the original

response_modes.reason: Drawing on text language as a resource requires students to build a repertoire of how story vocabulary, dialogue and description function. More retelling practice across more texts expands this repertoire.

success_criteria: Student includes at least two specific vocabulary items or language features from the original in their retelling
Student uses at least some language that goes beyond their own everyday speech

nodes.label: Adapting the story
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can adapt a familiar story — changing a character, setting or event — while maintaining the recognisable plot structure and using appropriate vocabulary.
nodes.minimum_width: Adapt at least one element of a familiar story (change a character, setting or event) and retell the adapted version orally or through drawing/role-play.
nodes.typical_width: Adapt familiar stories by changing characters, settings or events, maintaining the underlying plot structure and using vocabulary and language features appropriate to the story type, through oral retelling, role-play, drawing or digital tools.
wider: Adapt a story into a different medium — e.g. turn a written story into a role-play with dialogue
Adapt a story to a different cultural setting and discuss what changes in the language, characters and events

response_modes.reason: Adapting while preserving structure requires students to coordinate their understanding of plot, character vocabulary and text structure — it is the integration task that brings all three elements together in creative production.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Adapting stories across media (oral, drawn, digital) and exploring cultural transposition gives advancing students rich creative and analytical work — they must understand the story deeply enough to transform it.
success_criteria: Student's adaptation changes at least one element while maintaining the recognisable plot structure
Student uses vocabulary and language appropriate to the story type in their adaptation
